The coat corner

When the weather turned cold, our school opened a corner where students could borrow clean coats. On my first afternoon as a volunteer, I was asked to ____1____ them by size, making a separate pile for each group. I thought the job would be easy: find a suitable coat, lend it out and write down its number.

Then I noticed a boy standing near an ____2____ chair. No one was sitting on it, and there was nothing on its seat. He looked at the coats several times but did not come forward. When I offered to help, he ____3____ his head. I almost decided that he was only waiting for a friend. But as he turned to leave, he pulled his thin shirt more tightly around himself.

I followed him a few steps and spoke in a ____4____ voice so the other students would not hear. He explained that he needed a coat but did not want his classmates to know. Until then, I had considered only whether a coat was warm and the size was ____5____. I had not thought about how it felt to ask for one.

The next day, we moved the borrowing ____6____ into a small room beside the corner. Students could now speak to a volunteer away from the crowd. We also stopped calling names ____7____ when someone returned a coat. Instead, students showed us the number on its label.

A week later, the boy came back wearing a coat. This time, he ____8____ me before I noticed him. "Hello again!" he called. He had brought another coat from home that his younger brother had outgrown. He wanted to ____9____ it to the collection.

The corner still needed careful records and clean clothes, but I no longer saw those as the ____10____ parts of the service. A practical system could work badly if it ____11____ the feelings of the people using it. Listening to one student had helped us ____12____ a problem that our tidy lists could not show. We had not bought more coats or made the room larger. We had simply made asking for help less ____13____. That small change helped the boy feel ____14____, and it taught me to look beyond the object we were ____15____.

The orchestra became easier to lead when I stopped treating my own view as ____13____. Mira's comment had not reduced my responsibility.
